chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who dies and leaves behind his maternal uncle, his maternal aunt, his paternal uncle, his paternal aunt, his son, his daughter, his brother, and his sister. He (peace be upon him) said: 'All of these inherit and possess. So when the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt gather together, then for the paternal aunt is two-thirds, and for the maternal aunt is one-third.'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a paternal aunt versus a maternal aunt when both are present?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of simultaneous inheritance (tara'ud) among multiple collateral relatives, confirming that paternal and maternal aunts, along with siblings, can all inherit concurrently rather than excluding one another. It specifically resolves the distribution between the paternal aunt (ammah) and maternal aunt (khalah) by assigning two-thirds to the former and one-third to the latter, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the weight of paternal lineage in inheritance shares. This ruling is significant for understanding how Shia fiqh handles complex family structures where multiple branches of the family survive the deceased.
